utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is the case number IT-97-25-T, the Prosecutor versus Milorad Krnojelac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Examined by Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Lisica. Can you hear me, Mr. Lisica?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you started to describe what happened after Mr. Zekovic had escaped, and you mentioned that at some point in time you were locked into an isolation cell. Where was this isolation cell?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That isolation cell was right behind the reception area.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to show the witness Exhibit 6/1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please point out this isolation cell to us.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's this one where I'm pointing now with the pointer. Provided that this is the reception office, the reception desk, then it could be this. If this is the reception desk, then it's right behind.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The witness was pointing at the fifth room counting from the left side of the building, the room next to the reception office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you alone in this isolation cell?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I arrived there, when I was taken there, I found Berberkic or Berberovic. He was a tinsmith. He used to work with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he in the group that was beaten in the hall that you described yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the entire staff of the metalwork shop, and he was with us. There was a Berberkic who had been brought to that room. That's where I found him. It was a room with metal rings in it. It was taken over from the former KP Dom. It existed even before the KP Dom, while it was still a prison. That was their isolation cell, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see any injuries on Mr. Berberkic or Berberovic? Was he also beaten up?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a bed there, and he was lying there moaning. He was bent over. He moaned and cried.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay in this isolation cell?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every 15 minutes or so they would take me to the reception office, then take me back. Then they took us all up there to that building where the isolation cells are. When you enter the KP Dom on the right-hand side where the isolation cells are, I believe there are 10 or 12 isolation cells up there, and they took us to that corridor, that hallway. Some people were locked up in isolation cells, and I was told by Savo Todovic to lie down on the floor, and I did. He took his gun and pointed it against the back of my head, and he said -- since he knew my father, I have to say it the way he said it: "God damn your father Hasan. Tell me where Berberkic [as interpreted] is." Then he made me get up and he took me back to the isolation cell, where I found again this Berberkic. And during the night I was taken out every hour or so. But all the interviews I had were with Savo Todovic and Boro Ivanovic. Shall I continue?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wait a second. Just to clarify, maybe it's a mistake in the translation, maybe you misspoke. You said Todovic told you, "Tell me where Berberkic is." You probably meant Zekovic, right?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I had meant Zeka. Maybe I misspoke.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. While you were -- did you spend the entire night? Except for being taken out so often from the cell, did you spend one night in this isolation cell in the administration building?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was sometime before dawn, perhaps around 3.00 a.m. I was taken out for half an hour, then returned. And then the same thing repeated itself several times. And then for a while it was quiet, they didn't call me out any more, and when it dawned. In that isolation cell there is a barred window, a small window through which you can have a view of the Drina. I was watching some people moving around there, gathering. I knew some of them; some I didn't know. And then a guard came, shouting, "Warden, warden, we've caught Zeka." And I was glad in a way. Somebody then fired a shot or, rather, two shots. I don't know who that was. And after about a couple of hours, they took me out into the hallway, that is the censorship hallway, and that's where they started to beat me. And they wanted me to tell them the whole story, whether I had known that Zeka was going to run away and how he did it, et cetera, and they wanted me to tell the truth; otherwise, they would kill me. So I repeated the same story. They hit me on the head with their fists a little. Once they hit me and I hit this metal detector, this thing you pass through when entering. And then after that, they took me upstairs to an isolation cell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you looked out when you heard the shout, "Warden, warden, we found Zekovic." Did you actually see Mr. Krnojelac on that morning?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see Krnojelac. I saw other people. But at that moment I was watching through the window when one of them - I don't know who that was - when someone said, "Warden, warden," I think those were the words, "we've caught Zeka." And that's when I heard the shots. I assumed it must be Krnojelac who fired the shots, although I don't know, actually, because when you're looking through that window, you cannot see much. You can see -- you have a view at an angle of 45 degrees on each side. I didn't see much, really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that you were beaten after that on that morning. Who beat you?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of them was Pljevaljcic, and I know even the other man. I know his face, but I cannot recall his name right now. And while they were beating me, at that moment another one, Prodanovic, was sitting on a chair, across, and he said, "That's enough. Stop." That's about what he said. I don't remember the exact words. But they did stop. I had a scar here until recently.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When the witness said that, he was pointing at the left side of his face.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, Vlatko Pljevaljcic, he is number 35 on the list P3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this other person that you said you remember his face, was he also a guard?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was a guard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that you were then taken to the isolation cell upstairs. Which cell do you mean? Do you mean in the prisoners' quarters or in the administration building?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say upstairs. I said "up there," I think, but I'd like to correct myself anyway. It was on the inside of the KP Dom. They took me inside the building. When you're entering the KP Dom and when you go to the building on the right-hand side, that's the only place, actually, where there are isolation cells, and they were there from before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. And how long did you stay in the isolation cell after Mr. Zekovic was caught?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'll try to recount this briefly, if I can. Two hours later they took me outside again, and I went through an interrogation. There were four or five people there. I knew only one of them who had worked in Ozren company with me before, Vojo Starovic, and I knew the others' faces, but I didn't know their names. They interrogated me as to how come I have cigarettes, what kind of information I know -- I have, and then they took me back to the isolation cell. And perhaps another two or three hours later, a meeting was held. I don't even know whether it's proper to call it a meeting. All of us inmates were taken out into the yard. Rasevic came, Savo Todovic, several guards, and Mr. Krnojelac. To tell you the truth, I was in the second row. I don't know what I was thinking then. I was thinking about other things. I don't remember much. Somebody was giving a speech, I don't know who it was, but they said, "Here, we've caught Zeka. Of course we had to catch him. It's good that we've caught him," et cetera, et cetera. All I know is that Rasevic and Savo Todovic were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that Mr. Krnojelac was also there. How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I saw him, because they were standing there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that actually all members of the metalwork shop were mistreated related to Mr. Zekovic's escape. What about other people? If you look at the sheet in front of you, there is the person listed as number 73. Was he involved in this as well?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person under number 73 was designated by somebody to be something like the monitor of the room where we were. I didn't see it, but that same person told me, and other people had seen it as well, that guards were making the rounds upstairs and putting pressure on prisoners to tell them about Zeka, and that person, because he was the senior in that room, was also put under pressure. They told me that they had been abused, maltreated, too. To what extent, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After Mr. Zekovic was captured and after this speech was held in the yard, were you punished further on? Did someone punish the work crew members and others?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that a part of that crew was released, and Savo Todovic told me then that he would punish me with two months' solitary confinement and that I would not be working outside but exclusively, only, in the metalwork shop. And I think that I was actually in solitary confinement for 15 days or so only, and then I was returned to my room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Except for this incident with Mr. Zekovic, were you interrogated when you arrived in the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean on the 18th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean following the 18th of April. Were you interrogated at some point in time?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I gave a statement up there in May, I believe. Do you mean that, or do you mean what happened right after Zeka?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no. We are talking now about May, May 1992, when you "gave a statement up there." What does it mean, "up there"? Where were you? Where did you give this statement?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave that statement in the offices right behind the warden's office. Those were offices looking towards the back of the compound. I was invited there sometime in May. I wouldn't know the date. They were Vojo Starovic and Vladicic, whose first name I forget. And Vladicic -- actually, we were discussing how some people had reported lots of weapons in existence, and Telo Mustafa was mentioned. And he typed out a statement without even asking me much. He didn't even ask me. I knew this Vladicic from before, and he asked me to read it and to sign it, if I agree with it. I didn't even read it, actually. I just signed it and returned it to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you were -- you gave this statement in an office right behind the warden's office. Does that mean on the second floor, on the same floor as the warden's office was, or somewhere else in the administration building?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. If we take it that the warden's office is here, then it means on the inside. So it could be the second or the third room from the warden's building.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to show the witness the floor plan 6/3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you, could you point out where you gave the statement? This is actually the second floor.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This part here, approximately. This part here. Well, I can't say exactly whether it was, this one or that one, because I -- when I came there to give a statement, I didn't really count. But I think it's this area here. It's either of the two.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The witness was pointing at the two offices on the right side seen from the warden's office, and it says Upravna on the floor plan. It's called Upravna. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you mistreated during the interrogation?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they tell you what would happen with your statement or what would happen with you?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know, this Vojo Starovic told me while they were sitting there talking -- actually, Vladicic was the one who was supposed to finish this business with me, and since Starovic was there anyway, making his own investigations, the two of them shared an office. And he said that we would all be put into categories: Those who were loyal to the Serbian state would be released. Those who were against that state, all according to their lists, of course, would be punished, some more, some less. But it all boiled down to the fact that we would all be categorised, divided into groups. And I just remembered, I seem to have read on the top of my statement, "Muhamed Lisica is loyal to the Serbian state," or words to that effect. In any case, the essence was that we would all be divided into categories.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Starovic or Mr. Vladicic, did they tell you in which category you would be?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The most beautiful one, the first group, which was the best group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did they indicate who would make the decision? Were they actually making this decision that you were in the first group, or who?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in order to be able -- well, I actually couldn't define that, who would make the decision, but he was explaining that this decision would be made, that you would be categorised. And when he said that, he didn't say, "I would decide," and I didn't even ask him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever have a discussion about this grouping system, this categorisation with other members of the KP Dom staff?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know, I talked to a lot of Serbs who worked on the staff of the KP Dom, and it all came down to the same thing: You who are working will be protected; you have it easy; you are not guilty of anything. It all boiled down to that, that we were lucky, that it's very good for us that we were working, because we belong thereby to this good category.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember who said -- for instance, can you give us examples of guards or staff members who said that to you?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can remember. There are many of them, actually. I heard this story from Savo, from this Vojo, the interrogator. I think I was told the same thing by this tall man, Obrenovic. Well, most of them told me that. If I went guard by guard, then perhaps 40 or 50 per cent of them told me the same thing, that it's a good thing for us we were working. It's difficult to answer you precisely, but it all boils down to this categorisation. And now when you ask me what each of these groups mean, what do I know? The first group seems to be the best, the second is less good, and the third is the worst.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Savo said that to you. You mean Savo Todovic?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever discuss this matter with a guard Radovan Vukovic?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I talked to him in the beginning, when I was caught, because he was my next-door neighbour. And when he was -- when I was brought there, he was a guard on the inside, and he called me out, and outside the entrance. So I talked to him, and he said somebody from the neighbourhood would go to the command to take care of me, and he also said we would be divided into groups.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, this guard is Radovan Vukovic, is number 52 on the list P3, and the guard Obrenovic that the witness mentioned in this connection is number 46.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you were in the most favourable group, and you mentioned the group -- second group is less good and the third group is the worst. Did any guard or prison staff member ever indicate what would happen to the third group, people in the third group, or could happen to them?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's very, very difficult to define, but a fact that we all knew, all of us inmates in the camp, and even the prison guards, was that if the first group was going to be released, the second group was going to be punished with some prison sentence, then the third group would be in greatest trouble, would be given the harshest punishment. I don't know exactly what was meant by that. Perhaps a long prison sentence, perhaps something else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice that detainees were taken out for beatings?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did notice. They beat people. They took them out; they returned them. Some people were taken out and never returned. Some people returned with scars. It lasted from May until August. After that, it didn't happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We do not need to talk about all the detainees that were taken out, beaten, that you saw returned, because we have already heard a lot of evidence on this. But I would like to discuss a few particular incidents Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25 with you. Did you ever see, actually see with your own eyes, that people were beaten? Not that they returned with injuries, but that they were beaten, actually?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Once from Room 11 I watched, and when you are looking from Room 11 at an angle of 45 degrees down at the administration building, I think in that building first there was a toilet, a staircase, then some administrative offices, and then behind the toilet and the staircase there were rooms with windows half painted over, and they were broken in many places, the window panes. And when you look at this area from Room 11, at this angle, what I could see were persons up to the waist, Muslims. I was watching from there. I couldn't see the guards beating them. I could see the persons who were being beaten, looking at them -- looking down at them, because I was above them. And there I saw Kula. That's the name I knew him by. I think his first name was Mustafa. He was being beaten and slapped on the face while he was standing against the wall, but he wasn't standing inside the room. When you look at the room, there is a door. This door was open and it leads to the hallway, so that was happening in the hallway.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to show the witness Exhibit 6/1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you point out the room where the beatings occurred when you saw it?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is the building, if that is Room 11, it has two windows here, I think, two or three, and over here two or three. I have no idea whatsoever. I was in this room here. Here, one of the windows, when you look this way under an angle of 45 degrees directly here, into these rooms here - because I was here - you have a direct view of these rooms here. Now, if this is the staircase, if this is the toilet, then it was these rooms here, and this is where the hall is. And now there's a door here, right? One door, the other door. And now I could see, in this angle, up to the waist, the person who was being beaten and the persons who were doing the beatings. I had a direct view, face to face, of the person who was being beaten, while I saw the backs of the persons who were doing the beatings. That is one thing. The other thing is that I saw a lot of commotion here and also people kicking, and I couldn't see the floor, though.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I have to interrupt you because I have to tell for the record where you were pointing at. And if I understand you correctly, you were pointing at the room -- at the second room, counting from the left side of the administration building, next to the room where it says "Tel" in it; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "Tel." I don't know -- well, yes, yes. It's this room, yes, and this view from here. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me clarify. Did the beating that you saw, did you see it in this room where it says "Tel," that is, next to the toilet, or in the next following room?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know what, I didn't think about this, whether it was in this room or in this room, but it was in one of these two rooms. That I'm 100 per cent sure. I think - at least, that's what I think - it's in this room where it says "Tel." Now let me tell you a different story. When I see it from there, I did not really register this because there were lots of windows here. I could not exactly register. This is the room. It's precisely this Tel room that you are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. It's enough with the plan. Maybe it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that my learned colleague omitted to tell us for the transcript the place where he was looking from, and the witness also showed us that. He showed the right-hand side of building number 1, and I think that that should also be reflected in the transcript. He showed exactly where he was looking from, under which angle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I don't think that you could quite safely say it was the right-hand side. It was towards the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac and Your Honour, I just -- I wanted to use now the floor plan where we see Room 11 so that he can point it out to us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: -- So I was coming to this. For me it was not really obvious, because he was moving, and I always hear it later.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, now he is going to get a room that -- where it says number 11. He can't point number 15. He's going to point at number 11. This was a floor plan of the building where the room numbers are not marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, the Defence is entitled to have recorded what it was he was pointing at.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The problem that you and I suffer from is that we are hearing the translation, which is about half a sentence behind. But my impression was that he pointed first of all roundabout the middle, then moved towards the right.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But he wasn't at the right end, as Mr. Bakrac suggests, with all due respect to him, but it was to the right side of the building.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, if you want to have your view recorded differently, please say so, but -- because you were obviously hearing the witness at the same time as he was pointing, which is an advantage we don't have.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I fully agree with you. First he showed the middle part of building number 1, and then he started moving the pointer towards the right-hand side. I fully subscribe to your description. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We can proceed now with the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Is there now the map 6/2 in front of him? Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you see here a floor plan, and there are rooms in the prisoners' quarters indicated. Can you show us where you were when you saw what happened in the room marked as "Tel"? Where were you when you saw Mr. Kula being beaten?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this room. Sometimes I was in this room, sometimes I was in that room, but at that moment when I saw Kula, I was in this room, at this end here, right here, because I think -- I don't know. I've forgotten, but I think there are two rooms here, or three. And here, also, there are two or three rooms. I wasn't really counting them. So I was precisely in this room.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The witness was pointing at the right room in this protruding building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Part of Room 11, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, part of Room 11.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you pointed out where you were in Room 11 on this other sketch, you also moved your pointer to the right side. Did you also observe what was going on in the administration building from other windows than the one that you just indicated?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have to repeat all of this to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You said that you saw from this Room 11, this right-hand room, you saw what was happening in "Tel." Were you also observing what was going on from other sections of Room 11?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether others could see it or whether I could see it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You. You.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it could only be seen from this room and that room. As for the other rooms, you could not see it from there. While this was happening, I was going from this room to that room. I would watch it for about five or six minutes and then I'd leave, and then I'd take a little walk here and then I'd come to this room. But I spent most of my time precisely in this room, the one I'm showing you right now. Here. Here. Can you see the pointer?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The witness was again pointing at that same room, the right room from Room 11. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you recognised Mr. Kula Mustafa. Is it Mustafa Kuloglija?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he the only one that was beaten on this occasion when you saw what was happening?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know what, the month of May, the end of the month of May, in June and July, practically every day -- not every day, but almost every day, 80 per cent; I was not watching all the time. I don't know why. I mean, when I was personally watching, I saw Kuloglija Mustafa, Munib Veiz, and I only watched one single night. I did not watch during the night after that or the night before that. That's when I saw Kula. Because this view that you have from up here -- I'm afraid I'm going to make a mistake now in terms of metres, but it's not far away. It's not far away. You can actually see it, because where I was, the lights were turned off, and over there, the lights were turned on, so you could see. Then also another thing: If you could not see something, you know who was taken out and then you know who was beaten there. So I saw Kula being beaten and I saw Munib Veiz. Why did I see Munib Veiz? I saw his hand and I saw his wristwatch. He had a yellow wristwatch, and you could see quite obviously that it was his hand, and that's how I came to the conclusion that it was Munib Veiz.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that on the same night that you saw the hand of Mr. Veiz, Munib Veiz? Was that the same night?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall any other person that was called out on that same night at the same time?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kemo Dzelilovic, I think, Pasovic. Well, when I personally was watching, I think that they took out four or five persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned a person Pasovic. Is this Mensud Pasovic or does this person have a different name?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew him as Pasko, under the nickname of Pasko. He had a shop, and then later they told me Pasovic, but I don't know the name. I really don't know names.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, Munib Veiz is listed under C-28 and B-59. Kemo Dzelilovic is C-7 and B-19. Mustafa Kuloglija is B-35 and C-15, and we have a Mr. Pasovic, Mensud, listed under B-44, but I think we cannot be sure at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did these men return after this beating?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that you could see because the light was on. Was light on in the room, in the room -- in this room where the beating occurred?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was lit pretty well. Well, it was most probably in the room because it was lit pretty well. You could see well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it already dark outside?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the beaters? You said they were with their backs to you. Could you recognise any, nevertheless?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not recognise them, no. No, I did not. Usually all of them were military men, because they had quite a few camouflage uniforms and military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So those who beat were not the guards; they were military people?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally saw that they were not wearing KP Dom uniforms, that they had camouflage uniforms and military uniforms, military uniforms, right. But I actually saw a guard there, Burilo was his name, who was walking around there, but I didn't see him beating anyone. I'm telling you again: They had their backs turned to me, and I would see the person who was being beaten. I saw his face, so what could I see? Their backs from the waist upwards. The KP Dom uniform was some kind of bluish colour. I don't know that colour exactly. So it was quite different from the military uniform, so you could see that quite obviously. You could see whether it's a guard who was doing the beating or this other guy, or whether a KP Dom uniform was being worn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you mentioned that Burilo was there. Did you see him do anything?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Once I saw Burilo go up those stairs that are there in the drawing. He went and brought a blanket in his hands. I saw that. And now, if you can see a person down to the waist, then you can see that hands are being lifted this way in order to lift something. Now, you don't see what it is down there, but you see that this person is lifting something with his hands and obviously carrying something. Now, I could not see what he was carrying, because you see under a certain angle, so you see this part here. Or if he turns around, then you can see up to here, approximately. So then you can see by the movement of his hands what he is doing. You can assume what he is doing. So I saw that he was, like, lifting something, like lifting something difficult -- like lifting something heavy. And people were being beaten there, and also you could hear gunshots. So we said, "Oh, so they're carrying the Muslims out. They killed them and now they're taking them out."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you hear the gunshots?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was also after the beatings and all of that. That's when the gunshots were heard. Now, did the beatings go on for two hours and was it after two hours of all of this? I think four to six gunshots rang out, and after these gunshots, Burilo went to get a blanket and came back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you make out from where the gunshots came? Could you hear where it came from?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, listen. If you're standing in this Room 11, if you hear gunshots, then, as you were listening to that, you realise that it was coming from there. Now -- I mean, once, for example, I saw fire, fire coming out of a pistol, and then all the sounds reflected that it was coming from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean from this room "Tel," T-e-l?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Or the one next to it. Don't do this, please. I'm 90 per cent sure that it was from the "Tel" room, but, you know, there are quite a few windows there, and these windows are separated from one another. Perhaps there's the toilet, there's the staircase, and then these rooms. And now when you look from up here, I cannot tell you: Right, it is that room exactly. If I were to come to the KP Dom and if I were to be looking at that window, then I'd send you to that window and then I would tell you which room to go to and you would know for sure which room it is, because you can see that on the spot, actually. So it happened somewhere those three or four windows. So it's not the toilet, it's not the staircase, so it's the room next to the staircase.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to show the witness the photo 7473.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be able to point out the window to us? It's obscured. It's a little bit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: There is a better -- there's a better one than that, is there not, that you look right down from round about Room 11?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, but the problem is that we cannot see where the building ends on this other photo. That's the problem with these other photos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: But we -- the trees --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I would find it very difficult to see any windows there with the trees.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. It's difficult. Let's use the photo 7475, although you cannot see where the end is, actually, of the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's the one I had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Can we not locate where those two damaged portions of the wall are on the other photograph --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: -- so that you can see that the first window here is either the first window from the end of the building or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. We should have both photos in front of the witness. I think it's then easier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We can agree upon that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It would help the witness, no doubt, to have both Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25 there.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But am I right the first window you see is in fact the first window past the doorway into the administration block?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if you look at the upper photo first, you see there is a kind of -- after the first window, right under this number 1, there is -- no. It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I've just seen for myself. The window you see on the other photograph, the second one you showed him, was the second one from the door.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. You see there is a kind of renovated spot under number 1. Now if you look at the other photo, this photo, you have to have -- we have to have a wider -- we have to see more of the photo. Can you move it so that -- we need to see more of the photo, the entire photo, please. The entire photo. Yes. Stop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see here this same renovated spot, and can you, from now, looking at this, can you point out the window?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's these two windows. If this is the staircase, this is the toilet, this is the entrance, then it could be these windows here. If you're looking --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please --

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: These. These also. So it's probably these windows here, 1, 2, 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With --

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of those.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. The witness was actually pointing at the second and third window counted from the left side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you said -- actually, you pointed at the first window and said this is the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It was the second and third window from the right-hand side of the building that he pointed to. You see where the pipe, the drainage pipe goes down between the windows? He pointed to the one which is second to the right of that and third to the right of that. If you start from number 1 on the right-hand side, he pointed to the second and third from the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. That I wanted to say, didn't I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You didn't. You said to the left, that's the problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I confused left and right. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Are you left-handed?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I only ask that because my wife is left-handed and she always tells me the wrong way.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I often confuse it too, I'm sorry. I wanted to say "right." Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you said the third window on the left-hand side was the toilet, and this was not the toilet.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. We can put the photos away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, after you heard the shots and after you saw Burilo lifting something that you couldn't really see, did you hear anything else?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, then the beating affair was over and that's it; that was over. I heard, and I wasn't the only one - lots of us heard this - we heard the Kedi vehicle that we talked about earlier. We heard something being dragged, then we hear the car being ignited, and now we link all of this together. The Kedi is turned on and then you see when the Kedi is turned on, you see it's hard for it to get going. For example, I and all the mechanics know that if you put four men into a car or if you're in the car on your own and if you turn on the car, I know whether you have people in the car or whether you're there on your own. Perhaps it was about 15 minutes or so, and then the sound was interrupted. And now what I heard, that they could not turn the car on easily, was only because of the exhaust pipe. It was faulty. So then you could hear the way it worked. And after about 15 minutes, there was no more sound. After a while, I don't know, an hour or so - I don't know exactly - the sound could be heard again. It came to the KP Dom and then it disappeared again. That was over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, you mentioned that such incidents occurred on several occasions, but you watched it only once, the one time that you described to us. Did you hear beatings where you didn't see anything, but heard beatings?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, but what I heard I had to hear from the hall. When you enter number 11 -- first when you enter number 11, there is a hall, and then in this hall there is a toilet and a sink, and then that hall faces directly this window that you showed here in the picture. And then that should be the hall of the iron door. That's where I heard the moans and names being called out. I know which name: Nurko, Nurko. Somebody was yelling, "Nurko, Nurko, Nurko, wake up," and you could hear the moans.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, with the help of the usher, I would like you to look again at the floor plan 6/2. And can you point out --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We need to see the prisoners' quarters. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you point out the hallway you were, where you were when you heard these sounds?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This hall here. If this is within 11, I can't tell by this drawing of yours. One, two, three -- no -- yes. Yes. It's this hall here. And this hall here, exactly. This is that part. I think there's a window here, a window that was painted over, and that I actually heard these sounds from here, and this was actually taking place here. When I listened to this from here, when you come here or here, then you couldn't hear it that much. Somewhat less, I don't know why. And I was standing here. It wasn't only me; it was a few of us standing there, and we heard that, "Nurko, Nurko." We heard his moans, but we didn't know who was being beaten. However, since this other one was saying, "Nurko, Nurko," we realized it was some Nurko. Now, which Nurko, I don't know either, but it was Nurko.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The witness, in relation to his own position, was pointing at the hall in the set of rooms 11 below the WC and this other -- the other word is UMIV. And he was pointing at this passage, this hall behind the metal door, where the beating -- where the sounds came when he heard this "Nurko, Nurko." Yes. Thank you. Your Honour, the Prosecution believes that the witness is referring to Nurko Nisic. He is the only Nurko that was ever mentioned as being a victim, and that's C-19 and 5.27 in the schedules and in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you: Did you see or hear the Croat Krunoslav Marinovic being beaten?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard sounds made by other people, but whether it was precisely him, I don't know. I cannot recall right now, but he was in my room. I know when he was taken out, and when he was taken out, another man was taken out with him. Sounds could be heard then, moans. But whether it was Kruno's voice or not, I couldn't say with any certainty, but it couldn't have been anyone but the two of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall who was taken out together with Mr. Kruno Marinovic?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I cannot recall right now.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, the victim Marinovic is listed under C-17.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those victims that we had just mentioned, did you see any of them being beaten on another occasion, and did you see them return on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it happened on other occasions during interrogations, and after interrogations, those things would happen in the afternoon, just before dark. Another neighbour of mine was taken out, Ekinda, I believe his name was, Cedic. He was taken out, beaten up, and returned. They took out Dzemo Vahida, who was also in my room. He too was beaten up and brought back. I saw the scars on their faces. I cannot remember really. We had a rule there: The person who would return from a beating would never be asked about it. It could only be discussed 10 or 15 days later. But as far as this Ekinda is concerned and the other people who were with me in the same room, Room 11, they were lying next to my bed, and I saw the scars on their faces, and that's how I knew they had been beaten.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, Ekinda Cedic is listed under C-5, and Mr. Vahida Dzemo is listed under C-27 and 5.29.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These other victims that you have already mentioned, Mr. Munib Veiz, was he taken out on several occasions and did you see him return with injuries?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through a combination of circumstances, he came to Room 11 from upstairs where this group from Livade was incarcerated, and he was beaten, too. I could see the bruises on his legs and on his back. And once when he was taken out downstairs and when he came back, I could see that he had been beaten, but there were no signs of injury on his face. I don't know whether he had been beaten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Dzelilovic, was he also taken on several occasions and did he return being beaten?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember -- yes, he was taken out once, and he was beaten. There was a bruise here on his face, right here, but I don't know how badly he was beaten.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When the witness was saying that, he was pointing at his -- on the left side of his --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Forehead.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Forehead, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Konjo Halim, was he taken out and beaten?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Konjo Halim. It was right at the beginning when the camp was just established, and the boss there was still Slavko Koroman. I was listening to his interrogation and the beating. It could have been a Friday or a Saturday. On Sunday I went out with Slavko to work, and Slavko told me that Konjo had died, that the doctors had established that he had suffered a stroke and that he would have died anyway. And I also can say about one of the guards who didn't work in the KP Dom at all, I met him down there in the hospital, because I was building something which had to do with the morgue. It was in the hallway from the reception area to the morgue. And this guard told me that he was lying there in the morgue, that he had suffered a heart attack, that he hadn't died from the beating but that he had died from this heart attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see the body of Halim Konjo himself?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the morgue or where?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to the morgue myself. I saw the body there. I wasn't really very keen on looking closely whether it was him or not him, but a corpse was lying there and they told me it was Halim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you mentioned Mr. Koroman. He is on the list of employees as the number 32. And do you recall the other guard that mentioned him as well, the corpse, I mean? Do you know the name of this other guard?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't really say. I knew all the guards. Some of them I knew from before, but I cannot really recall now. I remember only those of the guards whom I had known from before, and I also remember the one who hit me, because he hit me. But I cannot really tell his name now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Do you know a Halid Konjo, and can you tell us what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew him very well too. He's also a native of Foca. He was taken out, allegedly to pick plums, and that's all I know as to where he had gone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Nail Hodzic, was he taken out and beaten?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nail Hodzic left completely on his own. He was in my room at the time. He left towards the end of that affair. I remember that he asked me for advice, What am I to do? A man called Pejic Boban came and asked him, and he was told, "Don't be afraid. You're just going for an interrogation. They will interrogate you and let you go," but he never came back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he was taken, did you hear also the sounds of beatings and screaming?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as for moans and screams, I don't know, but I could hear the interrogation; questions, explanations, answers. But I dare not say before this Court with any certainty whether I heard moans or screams; I couldn't really say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you hear or did you personally see his body or did you hear that some other detainees saw the body of this person, Nail Hodzic?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once this man Avdo told me - I don't remember his last name - who was going with another person to take these bodies to Foca, because I knew Nail Hodzic. He used to wear a cap and he had grey hair. This man said he knew Nail Hodzic and he pushed his body down the river. But I never saw him later, and I don't think he's alive really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to Avdo?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the real truth as to what happened, but I know that the International Red Cross came at that time from Trebinje and the chairperson there was Gordana and there was a fat American lady, and they told us that we can speak openly. The guards were not present. It was a rule that the guard would lock us up and leave. And I told him and other people, "Don't say too much. Keep quiet. God knows what might happen to us." After all, this Gordana woman was a Serb, and you never know. But he told a lot of things anyway, about this and that. And indeed, they did take him out after that and he never returned. I don't know whether it was coincidence. I don't know whether this Gordana woman told other people what he had said. But in any case ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that he said this and that. Did he actually mention that Mr. Nail Hodzic was killed or did he mention Mr. Hodzic when he spoke to the ICRC people?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, he did mention Hodzic and some other people. He even mentioned some people whose names I don't know, in fact, whom I don't know by name. And he said that he went to Foca on several occasions to push those bodies. It's not only I who heard this; it's other prisoners as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did it happen that Mr. Avdo told the Red Cross about Nail Hodzic and others, and the bodies of others? Was it in 1992 or later?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was 1993, but I couldn't give you the exact date. Because it was some kind of International Red Cross from Trebinje.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, the victim Nail Hodzic is mentioned under C-10. The guard Pejic Boban is listed under 91 in the employee list; and Mr. Avdo, we are not able to say his last name. We cannot identify him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in your previous statements you gave a lot of other names of victims, but I do not want to refer to all of them, because we have already heard a lot about these people. Just a very few others. Soro Seval, was he taken away in these beating incidents? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know he was taken away also on his own, but I don't know whether he was beaten.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: This person is C-24.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Alija Altoka, what can you tell us about him?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: About who?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Alija Altoka.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Omer and Alija Altoka, I don't know anything about the two of them, but I know they had left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Adil Granov?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know he was taken away, and I know that somebody said he had been informed on as owning a radio transistor, and he was taken out, but I don't know any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have -- yesterday you described to us that you cleaned blood of the Kedi. Was that timely related to these beatings that you described?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was washing away this blood. It could have been June when these isolation cells were being prepared. And all these events took place from May to August, the 15th of August. It was not in May or August, so it could have been in June or July. I think -- I cannot claim that it was human blood, but there had been beatings that night and I went later to clean those isolation cells, and I remember while I was doing it I was thinking that it was human blood, and I had heard that some corpses had been thrown into the river, so I put all those pieces together and that was the picture I got. That's my opinion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see bloodstains in the building, in the administration building, at that time?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That did happen sometimes, but since I had to lift my -- to put my hands up to be searched, there was a shelf behind me. I could put the things from my pockets there while they were searching me. And that was like bloodstains which had paled from frequent cleaning. It looked as if it had been washed before and the colour was paler. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to show the witness the photo 7470.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The bloodstains, did you see them in this hall, and if so, where?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my eyesight is not so good any more, but I noticed them here in this area and in this part here, because I was standing here with my hands up. And I stood for a long while and I had time to look. And here, you don't have this photograph here, where this censorship area and the detector, the metal detector, I saw most bloodstains here, so it could have been up to this door here. And for some length behind that door.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The witness was pointing on the left wall of this hall, and on the floor in front of this hall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you were also pointing at something that you cannot see, you cannot see on the photo.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we have the top photo? Can you --

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If anybody knows this area, when you start from here, this is the entrance into this room. Someplace here there is this metal detector, the censorship area. You have to go through this detector and behind the detector is this area that I'm talking about, where the bloodstains could be. It's difficult to explain now. If I could get there, I could explain easily on the spot. It's exactly the way you presented it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Let us see the photo 7446.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see bloodstains in this hall as well? The upper photo, please. Do you mean this hall?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This hallway. No. It was in the hallway we looked at before, at the very beginning of -- from this door here. It's in this hallway. When I would stop there, I could see the bloodstains.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, you saw it --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: 7470 again.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This area here, then this area here. This is approximately this detector door. So here a little, here a little, and this here, some of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. The witness was pointing at both walls, the right wall and the left wall, and also pointing at something further on that is not seen on the photo but belongs to that same hall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a part of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, but since we've already heard some descriptions, it's important for us to be reflected in the transcript that speaking about the right wall, the witness showed the border between the yellow paint and the blue paint, which is confirmed. So he showed some place in the middle of this wall.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This area here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And he was pointing to the left of the hat stand or coat rack, whatever it is there. There's a discolouration on the wall and it's on a corner and that's where he was pointing.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, these detainees who did not return, do you know what happened to them? Do you know if they are still alive?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you're asking me such questions. I was inside the camp. I don't know what happened, what was happening on the other side, but my information is that these people are missing, they're gone, they're killed. Kemo, for instance, Dzelilovic, he's a neighbour of mine. I know -- I contacted his wife, I know that he was never heard from again. Munib Veiz, I know him -- I knew him too. I contacted his friends. I know he was never heard from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of the prison staff members ever talk about these beatings?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know what you mean. Once this guy who was not a prisoner, he was a Serb, told me about these people who were his neighbours. He told me that at Previla he recognised the corpses of Suljo Soro and some man called Rasim Kajgana and some other corpses which he didn't know, and the people who he used to know were those same people. So it's something I heard from another person. I have no direct knowledge, if that is what you meant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear Mr. Relja Goljanin and Mr. Rasevic speak about Kemo Dzelilovic and what had happened to him?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I heard on one occasion that they were discussing -- but all this was happening in 1992 when we were very frightened. But it was precisely what you mentioned. It was something to the effect: We're sorry about these people. They were discussing it amongst themselves while I was working not far away. I think it happened in the hospital. I really cannot remember now. It's been a long time, seven or eight years. You forget even more important things. You forget even what you had for breakfast today. But I heard something to this effect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you ever -- did you ever hear -- overhear that someone talked to Mr. Rasevic about the killing of Muslims?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Do you think this --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Rather than go on with it, I think we may take the break now. We'll resume at 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you ever overhear someone talking to Mr. Rasevic about killings while you were sitting in a car?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, once. I was with the man under code number 144. I think we were on our way back from the hospital. For some reason we could not enter the KP Dom immediately because there was a group of soldiers in front of the KP Dom, so we waited. And then Sefko Kubat was sick. And Cedo, I think, Krnojelac, walked up to him. Now, was Rasevic the first to speak or Cedo, to say that Sefko Kubat was sick and that he should be taken to hospital? Cedo said to him, "We'll give him the brief procedure. Just take him to the bridge." Since I was sitting in the back, and also number 144 -- yes, number 144, he was sitting there with me -- Rasevic got a bit red and said he should do his job as he was supposed to do it and that he has been doing his job for 20 years already, professionally, and that he has nothing to do with such things. So they were sort of quarrelling. Their voices were a bit angry. And now, this Cedo Krnojelac, I did not see him, because this is a car, a Black Marija; you can't really see very well. I think this Cedo left. After that, in the meantime, we enter the KP Dom building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said Cedo Krnojelac. Was he an employee of the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was at the KP Dom, he did work at the KP Dom. He was not an official guard, as I knew the others to be. Was he employed only during the war or had he been employed there before the war, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have a Cedo Krnojelac listed under number 18 in the employee list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you couldn't see Mr. Cedo Krnojelac. How do you know, then, that it was him?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because Rasevic addressed him as Cedo. Since this Cedo Krnojelac is an elderly man. I think he's older than I am. Also, I recognised the voice. You see, when you talk to a person, you can also recognise him by his voice. I knew it was this Cedo because I did have contacts with him. He came to the metalwork shop several times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that Cedo said, "We'll give him the brief procedure. Just take him to the bridge." Did you understand what that meant?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that you understand right now what it means. I understood it to mean that he'd kill him and throw him in, whatever. You know what, in the later stages of 1994, that was in 1994, Serbs and Muslims started talking about such things, even by way of joking. Also, once, Goran Mitrasinovic came up and he said to this Glavonja, who was already mentioned, he said, "We're going to take Lija to the bridge," and then they would show something with their hand this way, see. And then Glavonja said, "What happened, happened." And that's what this man said too because Sefko Kubat, I think in 1994, died in the KP Dom. He was in the hospital and then he was returned from hospital because he had had surgery performed on him. And this one said to him, "Are we going to take him to the bridge where we've taken the rest," something to that effect, so I knew approximately what that meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Can you describe the action with the witness's hands, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. When the witness was talking about what should be done with Lija, he made a movement in front of his throat as slitting the throat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that what you meant? The movement that you did, was it like indicating a slitting of the throat?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know, this movement, among us, the Serbs and Muslims, it had a double meaning. When you show this, it means that you're going to kill him or that he's going to end his life or you're going to slit his throat. It's one of the three; but that's the point, that you will no longer be around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Witness, we heard from other witnesses already that detainees disappeared in exchanges, and I do not want to go into much detail on this, just a very few particular questions in relation to this. Did you ever observe detainees being taken for exchange while you were in the metalwork shop?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once I noticed that they brought a Furgon vehicle in front of the gate. I mean, the main administration building, the entrance into the main administration building. I was working at that time. It could have been around 11.00 in the morning. I was working up there on the roof, where the metalwork shop is, and this Furgon was perhaps a metre away, perhaps this far away. I don't know, perhaps a bit more. And I saw that these people were thrown into the Furgon just like this, and they were probably taken for an exchange or something. Because as for all the exchanges that took place in the KP Dom, I always did that, and then I would come in the evening and sometimes the Muslims would tell me yesterday 12 people left or yesterday 20 people left. So it's not that I really know about this, because I was not at the KP Dom itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that this Furgon was a metre away, from this entrance to the KP Dom; is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. It's not that I saw human faces very well, but, you know, if you were watching -- for example, I was looking this way. If the Furgon was facing in this direction, I would be watching it. If we were -- I was on the right-hand side. Also, it was in an angle and then you would see people getting in, right? Some even were being assisted to enter, sort of pushed in. You would see that. And then when you would come to the camp, then they would tell you 15 people were taken away yesterday. And then I remembered. I would link things up together. Yes, yesterday at 4.00 I saw these people entering the Furgon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know when, approximately when you would observe this?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that could have been the end of 1992. Because it's not very cold yet, but then on the other hand, it's not very hot either, so it could be October, November, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Zekovic also observe something similar, and do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was another occasion, not that one. Zeka and I had an assignment, and also Mr. 144, and I think 73 -- no, 73 was not there. We were making kiosks. The KP Dom was making kiosks. And Zeka climbed up on a kiosk. Thee kiosks were in the metal shop, that is to say between the two buildings. You had the picture there. Between the left and the right one. But they were more towards the right. And now he climbed up on the kiosk and I was down there, standing guard to see whether somebody would come. And at that time -- I think it was 1993. At that time, the guards were not that tense. They didn't guard us that attentively. And then he climbed up and then he was watching and then he told me the Furgon has been driven up, people are entering the Furgon, they are taking them somewhere. Zeka told me this. I was down there, I couldn't see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were ever members of the metalwork shop taken away for exchange? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, right at the outset, when the metalwork shop was established, there was an Uzeir Hadzalic who was working with me. I think that that Uzeir Hadzalic worked at the KP Dom before. I'm not sure. There was Munib Hadzic, or rather Hodzic; Suad Islambasic; then some Karahasanovic, nicknamed Karasi; then Avdo Kameric, I think, and some others. One morning -- or rather, they were taken in the evening. They were taken from the house, from the building, I mean, in the evening. And we went to work. There were four or three of us, and then there were 12 of us, approximately. And Relja said, "Where are the others? Where are they?" Because we would get into this metalwork shop, we would stand there, and then Relja would come out and give us our assignments. And where are they? And then I said, "They were taken out for an exchange." And he cursed, he said something like, "Oh, fuck them, they took away my best men." I think he said something brutal like that. And then he said write all of this down. And then Dule, one of the guys who was there, wrote all of this down. Actually, these people were taken away somewhere, but we don't know where, and I was really sorry that I was not in that group, because I thought that these people were being taken for an exchange, but actually, they were killed, I guess.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a result of these workers disappearing, what happened? How did Relja react to this? What did he do, except for cursing and being angry?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that I said that a few minutes ago. I can't remember now. He said, "They took away my best men." He cursed and he said to Dule, "Make a list of these guys who are still there." Oh, yes, right, you reminded me now. Then he said that he would go to the command to ask not to have the others taken away too, that he would go to the warden, he would go to the command, and say that we, the rest, should not be taken because he needs these people. This was 1992, when the KP Dom had all the materials needed, so he needed people to work. And I think we made 10 or 15 kiosks, I don't know. Perhaps I did not say everything word for word, but that is the gist of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that he said -- Relja said he would go to the command -- you said that he would go to the warden, he would go to the command. Did he say it this way? Did he mention the warden and the command? Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. You know what, at the KP Dom I personally know this, because I had contacts. Actually, people there, I mean, these guards, they didn't call anybody the director, the boss, or whatever. They said number 1, number 2, number 3, in line, sort of. So I guess the KP Dom had that before the war. And then man number 1 was --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please slow down. The interpreters cannot follow the sequence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Sir, you are stretching our interpreters beyond their endurance at the moment. Please speak more slowly. It is very hard for them to keep up with you.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. Man number 1, man number 2, man number 3, these were the persons that the guards respected too. Savo Todovic, Krnojelac, Rasevic, and some Miro Prodanovic, who was Rasevic's deputy. Relja Goljanin. Those were the people at the KP Dom who were in charge, right?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was: What exactly did Mr. Relja say? Did he say, "I have to go to the warden," or did he say, "I have to go to the command," or both? Do you recall? What exactly did he say?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is very hard for me to make a statement to that effect officially as to what he said, but he said, "I'm going. I'm going to the warden, I'm going to the command." Now, did he say, "I'm going to the command." And then, "I'm going to the warden," I don't know, whether he said one first or the other first, I don't know but he mentioned the warden as well; that he would go to the command to demand that his people not be taken away. It is hard for me to decide officially now he put it this way or he put it that way. But he said he would go to the warden and to the command did he say that he would go to see the warden and then the command or the command and then the warden, it's hard for me to say now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he actually do that? Did he go to the warden? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he inform you later on what was decided regarding his -- the members of the work group?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that your names were taken down when that had happened. Did you ever see a list with your name, later on, in the building?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED LISICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On one occasion -- now, I don't know whether it was after that, I think it was -- when I entered the building, precisely that picture, the hallway, where we were carrying out that censorship, there was a piece of paper and I saw it written there very nicely. At that time I was really pleased. It said the metalwork shop and then people's names listed.
