utterances.text: And you explained why you were beaten, the reason being that you had brought a radio into the KP Dom. Can you tell the Court how you were beaten on that day?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] -- look for the radio. I had to give it before entering the isolation cell. He beat me with his hands and feet. He kicked me into the cell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who discovered -- who from the KP Dom staff discovered that you had brought this radio into the prison?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: I'm not sure how come they knew the actual situation, how come I had a radio.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you were beaten, did anyone speak to you about the rules in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25 relation to bringing radios into the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: No. I was told about that after this had occurred. I was told about all the things that were forbidden to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who told you about these rules? Was it another detainee or staff at the KP Dom, or someone else?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Burilo, who had beat me. He said to me, "No more television, radio, newspapers, and all the rest."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive any injuries from this beating? Did it cause any bruises or bleeding or any other sort of injury?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Yes. I was bleeding then in the isolation cell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that Burilo beat you in front of the isolation cell. Was that the only place that he beat you, or did he beat you in other parts of the KP Dom as well?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: No. Only in front of the entrance into the isolation cell, because I was in the room right in front of the isolation cell. It was called number 16.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that you were beaten in front of the isolation cell, was that on the ground floor or a first or second or third floor?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Ground floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that isolation cell, was that in the building, in one of the buildings where Muslim detainees were kept?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. The same entrance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anyone else beaten with you at that time by Burilo, or were you beaten by yourself?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: No. I was the only one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after you were beaten, were you placed in the isolation cell?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you arrived in the cell, were there any other detainees in it?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what other detainees were in the cell? Who were they?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Suad Dervisevic, Dzamalija Juso, and Zaim. I don't know his last name. He's from Tjentiste.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you know Suad Dervisevic from before the war?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Yes. We were schoolmates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Juso Dzamalija, did you know him from before the war?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were placed in the isolation cell, did you notice anything about each of those people, whether in fact they had any injuries or whether or not they were perfectly healthy?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: They had been beaten. They had injuries. Juso Dzamalija lost conscious -- regained consciousness, lost consciousness again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What -- do you remember the particular injuries that Juso Dzamalija had when he was placed -- when you were placed in the isolation cell?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: I cannot remember. It was night-time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did all of the other detainees in this cell, did they all have injuries, or was it just one or two of them?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] -- isolation cell number 2. That is to say that we were all beaten and we all had lighter injuries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived at the cell, did Juso Dzamalija tell you how he was beaten and who beat him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Suad Dervisevic, did he tell you who beat him and how he was beaten?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: He had been brought from Trebinje. He was beaten all the time. But I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Zaim --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do apologise. I am following all of this because of the protective measures, but I heard the witness say he was beaten all the time, and here it says he was beaten all the time while he was travelling from Trebinje. That could be misinterpreted, as it was in the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, it is very difficult to hear the witness. THE COURT: The interpreters have just said they're having trouble hearing the witness, but what do you say he did say?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That he had been beaten all the time as he was coming from Trebinje, and on the basis of the transcript, one might conclude that he was beaten all the time when he came into the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All right. Well, thank you. I think we've now got it clear. Have you moved the witness closer to the microphone? Thanks. Would you mind speaking up, please, sir. The interpreters are having difficulty hearing you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know whether these three people in the isolation cell, whether they had been beaten inside the KP Dom or whether they had been beaten before they arrived?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: From the very moment of their arrest and until they were brought to the isolation cell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that Juso Dzamalija had lost consciousness. Was that whilst you were in the isolation cell with him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you or any of the others in the isolation cell receive any medical treatment for the injuries that you had and the ones that they had?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many beds were in this isolation cell?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not understand the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Would you get him to repeat it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if you could just repeat your answer. They couldn't hear you, the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: One bed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after you arrived in the isolation cell with the other three, did you sleep that night?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you sleep?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: On the floor of the isolation cell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sometime during that night, were you woken up?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you woke up, what did you discover?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Juso Dzamalija was hanged. He was hanging from a pipe of the water drain and he was lying on the makeshift toilet, which is actually a hole in the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "he was hanging from a pipe of the water drain," what was he hanging by?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: It's used to flush this squat-down toilet. It's the device for flushing. It releases water to flush the toilet, this squat-down toilet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he have anything tied around his neck?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: A belt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you discovered him, was he alive or dead?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That might need some elucidation, Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I assume you meant that, when you discovered him, he was dead.

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how, how he died? Do you believe that he took his own life?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: I can't give you an exact answer, because there was no autopsy, there was nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to his body?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: We carried it out, wrapped in a blanket, and loaded it onto a car within the compound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who the guard was on shift that night outside of the solitary confinement cells?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: No, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who carried the body outside of the cells and towards the car?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Suad Dervisevic, myself, and Zaim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once the body was discovered, did you call the guards?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did they say with the situation that they were confronted with?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: I cannot explain that to you. I don't remember it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the guards help you take the body to the car?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And whose car was it that Juso Dzamalija's body was placed in?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether it was an official car or whether it was a private car with no apparent markings on it?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other than the three of you who took his body to the car, did anyone else assist with the placing of Juso Dzamalija in the car or in finding out what happened to him? Was any medical treatment sought, even though at that stage he was dead?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long was Juso Dzamalija's body in this cell before you took it to the car?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: I don't know; I was asleep.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you discovered that Juso Dzamalija had died, how long had he been in the cell before you took him to the car?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: It was not even 20 minutes before the guards came in to unlock the door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was any inquiry made in relation to Juso Dzamalija's death? Were any questions asked of you about how he died?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you first arrived in the cell, did Juso Dzamalija tell you anything about how he was feeling before he died?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, in relation to the injuries received by Juso Dzamalija when the witness arrived in the cell, he's referred to in the schedules in B-17, B-17, and in relation to the guard Burilo it's P3, the list number 56.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you mentioned that you were beaten on two occasions. Can you tell us what happened on the second occasion that you were beaten.

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Yes. I worked, after the solitary confinement, on the upper side of the KP Dom. I was working with concrete, making ducts in the concrete. I was very hungry. I was begging the guard to let us go and have supper before time, because I was entitled to an extra meal. Since I was much too hungry, when my room left for dinner, I joined the group again. The guard saw me when I was collecting my meal, and he didn't say anything, at least then, but afterwards, when we were taken back to our rooms, he locked me in the room and told me to wait. Jasmin Sudar was there with me. He's a man who had worked with me that whole day. They beat us badly that time, breaking our bones, and after that, we were locked up in solitary confinement again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this beating after Juso Dzamalija's death?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about how much later? About how many weeks after that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: It was a month's interval.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did both you and Mr. Sudar, did both of you receive two meals that day?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the person or the people that beat you up on that occasion, yourself and Jasmin Sudar?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: I can't tell you. I didn't know any guards. It was at the beginning, and we got to know the guards only later, but then we got to know them very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you mentioned that when you were beaten, that bones were broken. Were bones in fact broken? Can you describe further the injuries that you got?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: That's not exactly what I meant. I didn't mean literally breaking our bones. They punched out our teeth, they would punch us in the stomach, kick us. They would punch us in the stomach, expelling the air from our lungs. They would beat us badly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these beatings, did they occur in front of the isolation cell?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this in front of the same isolation cell that you were previously in with Juso Dzamalija?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people beat you on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: I can't tell you exactly how many. I was so scared, and in such situations you only think about whether you're going to survive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this beating cause any cuts or bleeding?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Nose bleeding, yes. After a year passed, I didn't suffer any other consequences.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you notice the injuries that Jasmin Sudar received on that day?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: We were both beaten approximately the same. We had roughly the same injuries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after you were beaten, you were placed into the isolation cell; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long did you stay in that cell for after you were beaten?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: The next morning, I went straight to work, immediately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after the first -- going back to the first time that you were placed in the isolation cell with Juso Dzamalija, how long after he died were you kept in that cell?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Four days.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If I can ask the usher to put on the overhead projector Prosecution Exhibit 6/2A, which is the plan of the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, this is a plan of the ground floor of the detention facilities which the Muslim detainees were kept in the KP Dom. If you can look at the plan. Are you familiar with the layout, and would you be able to locate the place where the isolation cells were that you were kept on both occasions?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Yes. I know that drawing and I can point the place on it. This is the room where I was. This is the command where the guards were. This room here is solitary cell, solitary cells 1, 2, and 3. Actually, I was in solitary cell number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness was pointing to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. The witness was pointing to solitary cell 2, on the right-hand side of the right wing of the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, was the cell that you were placed in, was that -- was the window facing the front or the yard of the KP Dom, or was it facing the rear, the rear yard of the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: The windows faced the courtyard. They actually looked towards the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I can ask you to look at the plan again. Can you have a look closely at the solitary confinement cells on the right-hand side. And look again as to which location you believe you were kept on those both occasions.

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: I was in solitary cell number 2. That's the one. The windows looked into the courtyard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you said that the windows looked into the courtyard, and I think you also said earlier that the windows looked towards the canteen. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on that plan, can you point towards the canteen?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I know that it's difficult for the interpreters, it's difficult for me too, but the witness didn't say it's true. He said, "It's the same." And I see him nodding in approval.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "For me too," is what he meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You may one day have to explain to me the difference, but anyway, we now have an agreement from the witness. Yes, Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many solitary confinement cells were there at the KP Dom when you were there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Three on the lower side, looking towards the kitchen; three on the upper side, where I was, facing the outer wall -- sorry, the upper part of the wall of the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were in the cell facing towards the kitchen; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honours, I ask that the witness be shown Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25 photograph 78, which is from P18. The ERN number is 00407518.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps if you could put on the ELMO the bottom photograph. I've just been corrected, Your Honour. The photograph number is 7519.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, looking at this photograph, is this familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise for interrupting frequently, but I've just checked the transcript again. The witness had said cell number 2, but our colleague, Mr. Smith, did not explain for the transcript what the witness had pointed with a pointer on the previous photograph. I think it should be reflected in the transcript that he indicated cell number 2 on the rear side of the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think that's the only one that bears that number, but anyway, I think we can all say it's certainly what he did do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: That's agreed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, looking at the photograph --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, looking at the photograph on the screen, is that familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what does that show you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Solitary cell number 1, solitary cell number 2, where I was, and solitary cell number 3, from which you can see nothing. As for solitary cell number 2, it's facing the window. You can see the courtyard and the entrance into the kitchen, both entrances. From solitary cell number 1, you can see also the entire courtyard, the entrance into the canteen, where the Muslims ate on one side, on the lower side, and the Serbs ate on the upper side. And you can see all the way --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'll just slow you down for one moment. The questions and answers need to be translated and you're speaking a little bit fast for the translation. So I'll just have to record what you have pointed out, for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness pointed to cell number 2 and then brought the pointer across to the right-hand side towards the windows when he stated that the windows faced towards the canteen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, on the first occasion when you were placed in the isolation cell, was that cell number 2?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Number 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the second occasion that you were placed in the cell, after you were beaten for having two meals, was that also cell number 2?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If I can ask the usher to place photograph 80, which is numbered 00407521 from Exhibit P18, onto the overhead projector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, is that photograph familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Yes. That's the cell with the toilet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was a toilet similar to this in the cell where you were kept when Juso Dzamalija died?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Yes. They're all the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And looking at that toilet, you mentioned that Juso Dzamalija hung himself from some sort of mounting coming off the wall. Can you indicate on that photograph where Juso Dzamalija was hanging himself from?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you place the pointer on the photograph to your right?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness indicates the tap or lever on the left-hand side of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Can you tell us how far that was above the ground?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far was that above the ground, Witness?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: One metre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you found Juso Dzamalija's body, how was he sitting or standing when you came into the cell, into the toilet area?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: Many were thrown out behind those solders at this location, here. So the body and the legs were sort of pushed down the squat-down toilet. They were inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw him, was he seated or standing?

utterances.speaker: FWS-250
utterances.text: No. Just a couple of -- just a short distance further and he would be sitting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, I think we'll come back tomorrow morning. We'll adjourn. We resume again at 9.30 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 4th day of April 2001, at 9.30 a.m.
